prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck—what’s best depends on the facts of your case, how seriously you’re injured, whether it’s likely to go to trial, and how comfortable you are with the lawyer. I can help you find the right lawyer for your situation. Here’s how to choose one and next steps to take.

How to find a strong car wreck lawyer in Houston
- Look for relevant experience: attorneys who handle auto collisions and serious injury cases regularly (not just occasional PI work).
- Trial experience or board certification: lawyers who have tried cases are more likely to get better settlement offers. In Texas, board certification in personal injury or civil trial practice is a plus.
- Track record: past settlements and jury verdicts for car wreck cases similar to yours.
- Resources: firms that can pay medical liens, hire accident reconstructionists, and sustain a case if it goes to trial.
- Communication and availability: someone who answers questions promptly and explains strategy clearly.
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency—ask the percentage and whether costs are advanced and deducted only if you recover.
- Client reviews and discipline history: check online reviews (Avvo, Google) and the State Bar of Texas for complaints or disciplinary actions.

Where to look
- Texas State Bar lawyer referral and directory
- Harris County Bar Association referral service
- Online directories/review sites (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google), but use reviews as one data point
- Recommendations from medical providers or friends/family who had similar cases

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car crash cases like mine have you handled?
- What was the outcome (settlement/verdict) and can you give examples with similar injuries?
- Do you try cases or settle most before trial?
- Who will work on my case day-to-day (attorney, paralegal)?
- What percentage do you charge if we recover? Who pays costs if we don’t win?
- How long do you expect my case to take?
- How will you communicate with me and how often?

Important practical steps now
- Get medical care and follow treatment—documented injuries are essential.
- Preserve evidence: police report, photos, dashcam, witness contacts.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the insurance company without your lawyer.
- Be aware: Texas generally has a two-year statute of limitations for personal injury claims (act quickly).

If you want, tell me:
- your ZIP code or neighborhood in Houston,
- a brief summary of the crash and injuries,
and I can suggest several local firms or help you draft a list of questions to use in consultations.
